Usage: pty list [--json [--clients] [--strict]] [--tags] [--filter-tag k=v] [--remote [<peer>]] [--status <s>] [--summary]

List sessions (alias: pty ls). User tags show by default.

Flags:
  --json               Emit JSON
  --clients            With --json: add each running session's attached clients
                       (asks every daemon; ignored without --json)
  --strict             With --json: emit a per-root inventory envelope; exit 3
                       if incomplete (incompatible with --summary and --remote)
  --tags               Include internal bookkeeping tags (ptyfile*, strategy.*)
  --filter-tag k=v     Only sessions with the tag (repeatable, ALL must match)
  --remote <peer>      Also list a fabric peer's sessions (over fabric; the peer
                       runs 'pty remote-serve' exposed as 'fabric expose pty-remote')
  --remote             Bare (no peer): include pty-relay hosts (when installed)
  --status <state>     Filter by status: running | exited | vanished
  --older-than <dur>   Only sessions older than a duration (e.g. 30m, 2h, 3d)
  --newer-than <dur>   Only sessions newer than a duration
  --summary            Print a one-line count summary instead of the list

Strict inventory:
  Root is resolved from --root, PTY_ROOT, or the default and returned verbatim:
  no canonicalization; path aliases (including symlinks) are not folded.
  Retained metadata and tags are included regardless of lifecycle, subject to
  the selected filters. Recorded generation, daemonStartToken, and recovery
  processStartToken are exposed when present; ordinary --json is unchanged.
  Refused sockets without corroborating dead-PID evidence are incomplete
  (entry-unreadable). Non-regular companions are unreadable, never waited on.

Examples:
  pty list
  pty list --remote example-host
  pty list --filter-tag role=web --json
  pty --root /var/lib/pty list --json --strict
